title: Discrete order inside Heyting arithmetic

based_on.title: From Constructive Mathematics to Computable Analysis via the Realizability Interpretation (doctoral thesis)
based_on.pages: §1.3.2 printed p.25, HA definition only; elementary internal developments supplied locally

summary: Construct native HA order proofs from additive witnesses, including successor initial segments, trichotomy, internal decisions, and preservation and reflection under addition.
abstract: An inequality such as x plus a being at most y plus a ought to let us cancel a. Inside Heyting arithmetic, this requires a finite proof about the formula expressing order, rather than an appeal to the usual natural numbers. We express a non-strict inequality by an additive witness and prove the discrete order laws from the arithmetic equations. One induction constructs comparison for every pair, so both strict and non-strict order have internal decision disjunctions. The formulas for successor bounds describe exactly how a finite initial segment grows, while cancellation preserves and reflects the same witnessed inequalities at arbitrary arithmetic terms.
